0.headline: Stainless steel products maker Jay Jagdamba files updated DRHP to raise Rs 600 crore through IPO
0.heading: Stainless steel products maker Jay Jagdamba files updated DRHP to raise Rs 600 crore through IPO
0.intro: Jay Jagdamba IPO | The public issue will also include an offer for sale of 1.5 crore equity shares by promoter entity Floral Life Pte Limited.
0.body:
Jay Jagdamba, the Maharashtra-based stainless steel products manufacturer, has filed an updated draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to raise Rs 600 crore through an initial public offering (IPO).

The IPO will also include an offer for sale (OFS) of 1.5 crore equity shares by promoter entity Floral Life Pte Limited, a Singapore-registered company founded by Hari Prakash Malpani, according to the updated DRHP filed on August 24, 2026.

The company may also consider raising up to Rs 120 crore through a pre-IPO placement before filing the red herring prospectus with the Registrar of Companies. The pre-IPO placement will form part of the fresh issue, and the size of the fresh issue will be reduced accordingly if the placement is completed.

Jay Jagdamba operates two manufacturing facilities in Palghar, Maharashtra, and has four broad product segments: ingots and billets, rolled and bright products, flanges, and seamless pipes.

Its products are used across industries including consumer goods, oil and gas, automotive, infrastructure, medical equipment, machine components, data centres and petrochemicals.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Where will Jay Jagdamba use IPO proceeds?

The company plans to use Rs 450 crore of the net fresh issue proceeds to repay certain outstanding borrowings. Its total debt stood at Rs 1,433.2 crore as of June 2026.

The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

Jay Jagdamba entered the capital markets by filing its DRHP through the confidential route in June 2025. SEBI subsequently approved the draft papers in January 2026.

Jay Jagdamba reports strong FY26 performance

The company competes with listed peers including Ratnamani Metals and Tubes, Mukand, Scoda Tubes, Suraj and Welspun Specialty Solutions.

Jay Jagdamba’s profit surged 62.7 percent year-on-year to Rs 261.9 crore in the year ended March 2026, while revenue from operations increased 44.1 percent to Rs 3,162 crore.

Elara Capital (India) has been appointed as the sole merchant banker to manage the Jay Jagdamba IPO.

1.headline: Pernia’s Pop-Up Shop owner Purple Style Labs to launch Rs 680 crore IPO on August 31
1.heading: Pernia’s Pop-Up Shop owner Purple Style Labs to launch Rs 680 crore IPO on August 31
1.intro: Purple Style Labs IPO | The public issue, which comprises entirely a fresh issue component, will remain open for subscription until September 2.
1.body:
Purple Style Labs, the Mumbai-based luxury fashion company that operates the multi-brand, omnichannel fashion platform Pernia’s Pop-Up Shop, will open its maiden public issue of Rs 680 crore for subscription on August 31.

The IPO, which comprises entirely a fresh issue, will remain open until September 2. The price band is expected to be announced in the next couple of sessions.

The company has increased the issue size from the Rs 660 crore planned when it filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) in September 2025. The draft document received SEBI approval in January 2026.

The anchor book will open for a day on August 28. The IPO share allotment is likely to be finalised by September 3, while Purple Style Labs shares are expected to list on the stock exchanges on September 7.

Purple Style Labs offers curated luxury fashion from 1,109 active designer brands, including Seema Gujral, Anushree Reddy, Amit Aggarwal, and Rohit Gandhi and Rahul Khanna. Its product categories include womenswear, menswear, jewellery, accessories and kidswear.

Where will Purple Style Labs use IPO proceeds?
Purple Style Labs launched its first luxury fashion experience centre under the Pernia’s Pop-Up Shop brand in Mumbai in 2018 and has since expanded to 14 experience centres globally. Of these, 12 are in metropolitan cities across India, while one each is in London and New York.

The company will invest Rs 371.1 crore of the net IPO proceeds in its subsidiary, PSL Retail, towards expenditure on lease liabilities for experience centres and back-end offices in India.

Another Rs 138.9 crore will be spent on sales and marketing, with the remaining proceeds earmarked for general corporate purposes.

Who are the investors in Purple Style Labs?
Promoter Abhishek Agarwal owns a 26.09 percent stake in Purple Style Labs, while public shareholding stood at 73.66 percent, according to the red herring prospectus filed on August 24.

Akash Bhanshali-sponsored Volrado Venture Partners Fund II holds a 2.79 percent stake, followed by Madhusudan Kela-backed Singularity AMC’s Singularity Growth Opportunities Fund I with 1.86 percent. Investor Mukul Mahavir Agrawal holds a 1.37 percent stake.

Purple Style Labs remains loss-making
The company’s financial performance has been inconsistent and it remains loss-making.

Purple Style Labs reported a net loss of Rs 285.3 crore in FY26, widening from Rs 188.3 crore in FY25 and Rs 47.7 crore in FY24.

Revenue grew 13.9 percent year-on-year to Rs 557.8 crore in FY26. However, revenue had declined 2.9 percent year-on-year to Rs 489.9 crore in FY25.

Axis Capital and IIFL Capital Services are the book-running lead managers for the Purple Style Labs IPO.

2.headline: China's IPO rush is showing strain with pace nearing 2023 frenzy
2.heading: China's IPO rush is showing strain with pace nearing 2023 frenzy
2.intro: Investor enthusiasm has so far been buoyant enough to absorb the barrage of offerings. But as momentum in tech begins to fade, the market’s ability to take on fresh supply is being tested.
2.body:
China’s high-powered market for initial public offerings is showing signs that its breakneck pace could be difficult to sustain.

Fueled by enthusiasm for all things artificial intelligence, companies are raising money at the fastest rate since 2023, with volumes at levels just before cooling measures back then ushered in a multiyear lull. Recent high-profile deals have struggled to hold on to initial gains, while a robust IPO pipeline has reanimated liquidity concerns. And some highly anticipated deals may be taking longer to come to market than previously thought.

Since the beginning of July, proceeds have exceeded 119 billion yuan ($17.7 billion), more than the 114 billion yuan in the third quarter of 2023. Three years ago, that milestone marked a turning point in China’s IPO market. As Beijing pledged to boost capital markets, regulators also moved to curb the IPO frenzy to address concerns about liquidity drain. The measures effectively applied brakes to earlier reforms that had made it easier for companies to list.

Investor enthusiasm has so far been buoyant enough to absorb the barrage of offerings. But as momentum in tech begins to fade, the market’s ability to take on fresh supply is being tested.

“Since the AI trade rolled over in June, liquidity has been draining from the market,” said Yang Tingwu, fund manager at Fujian Tongheng Investment. “Mutual funds, quants and retail investors alike have little capacity nor appetite to add, and state-backed funds have largely been net sellers. In a market without incremental inflows, this level of IPO issuance is hard to digest.”

China’s stock market, along with Hong Kong, has emerged as the engine of fundraising for the AI buildout, with companies racing to sell shares as they look to expand capacity and compete with mostly US competitors. With deals such as CXMT Corp.’s near-record share sale, IPO proceeds this year have surpassed $30 billion for the first time since 2023, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

To be sure, large IPOs are coming to the market beyond the CXMT deal, which alone accounts for almost a third of the total fundraising. Unitree Robotics made its Shanghai debut last week, while China Resources New Energy completed the largest listing in the history of the Shenzhen exchange.

And in closely watched upcoming deals, Shanghai Enflame Technology Co. is proceeding with an IPO, while flash memory maker Yangtze Memory Technologies Co.’s application to raise 33 billion yuan has was accepted for review by the Shanghai Exchange on Friday.

So far, there’s been no official communication to indicate that authorities are preparing a clamp down on IPOs. And in contrast with the wave of 2023 deals, many of the largest offerings are tied to strategic sectors such as semiconductors and AI, which have heavy capital needs. Authorities have also made it clear that they will continue to support high-quality tech firms including homegrown large language models to list.

Still, signs of fatigue are emerging. Nearly a third of this quarter’s listings have lost more than half their value from post-debut peaks. Unitree is down 45% from its intraday high recorded during its blistering first day of trading.

Regulators may already be signaling discomfort with the pace of activity. Local media reported that exchanges recently met with brokerages to discuss the quality of IPO filings. Authorities have so far haven’t reacted to the reports.

And while YMTC is seen as a strategically crucial player in China’s tech self sufficiency drive, much like CXMT, the company didn’t go through an accelerated listing process like its larger rival. Currently, there are no deals taking the expedited route, which has only been used by CXMT and Unitree so far.

“Keeping up this pace would seriously damage the market’s risk appetite, said Yang at Fujian Tongheng. “Fortunately, regulators still control the tempo and can make adjustments if needed.”
